<div class="gt">
<p class="gt-lead">Pick a way to tune, then follow the steps one string at a time. The fretboard shows where to put your fingers; click any
spot on it to hear that note. No guitar knowledge needed: strings are numbered <b>6</b> (the thickest, nearest your chin) to <b>1</b> (the thinnest),
and frets are counted from the end where the tuning pegs are.</p>

<div class="gt-king"><b>Your ear is the tuner.</b> Every method here asks you to <i>listen</i>: to two notes agreeing, to a wobble slowing
down, to a chord sounding sweet. The microphone reading is there to check your ear, not to replace it. With <b>Ear first</b> ticked it stays
blurred until you've said what you hear. Start that habit today: musicians who only tune by looking at a screen can't hear when they've drifted
out of tune halfway through a song.</div>

<div class="gt-card">
  <h3>1. Your guitar and how you'll tune it</h3>
  <div class="gt-row">
    <label for="gt-tuning">Tuning</label> <select id="gt-tuning"></select>
    <label for="gt-a4">A =</label> <input id="gt-a4" type="number" min="415" max="466" step="1"> <span class="gt-lab">Hz</span>
  </div>
  <div class="gt-row" id="gt-custom" hidden>
    <label for="gt-custom-in">Your tuning, lowest string first</label>
    <input id="gt-custom-in" type="text" size="26" placeholder="D A D G A D" spellcheck="false">
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" id="gt-custom-go" type="button">Use it</button>
    <span id="gt-custom-say" class="gt-keys">Note names, or with octaves (C2 G2 C3 G3 C4 E4). Notes below about D2 are too low for the microphone reading.</span>
  </div>
  <div class="gt-methods" id="gt-methods"></div>
</div>

<div class="gt-card">
  <h3>2. One string at a time</h3>
  <div class="gt-steps" id="gt-steps"></div>
  <p id="gt-say"></p>
  <div id="gt-board"></div>
  <div class="gt-row">
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" id="gt-prev" type="button">← Back</button>
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary" id="gt-play" type="button">▶ Play reference</button>
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" id="gt-together" type="button">▶ Both together</button>
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" id="gt-next" type="button">Next string →</button>
    <label for="gt-vol">Volume</label> <input id="gt-vol" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="55">
  </div>
  <div class="gt-row" id="gt-drone-row">
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" id="gt-drone" type="button">Drone: off</button>
    <span class="gt-keys">on <b id="gt-dnote"></b>, an octave under the string; follows the step</span>
    <label><input type="checkbox" id="gt-fifth"> add the fifth</label>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="gt-card">
  <h3>3. Check your ear</h3>
  <div class="gt-row">
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" id="gt-listen" type="button">Listening: off</button>
    <label><input type="checkbox" id="gt-earfirst"> Ear first (guess before you see)</label>
  </div>
  <div class="gt-read" id="gt-read">
    <div id="gt-r-note" class="gt-r-note">–</div>
    <div><div class="gt-meter"><div id="gt-r-dot" class="gt-dot" style="left:50%"></div></div><span id="gt-r-cents"></span></div>
    <div id="gt-r-say"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="gt-row" id="gt-guess">
    <span class="gt-lab">What do you hear?</span>
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" data-g="flat" type="button">Flat (too low)</button>
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" data-g="in" type="button">In tune</button>
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" data-g="sharp" type="button">Sharp (too high)</button>
  </div>
  <p id="gt-msg" aria-live="polite"></p>
  <p class="gt-keys">With speakers, the page's own reference and drone reach the microphone too: stop them, or use headphones, when you check.
  Keys: Space reference, ← → strings, d drone, m microphone.</p>
</div>

<div class="gt-card">
  <h3>Tips that apply to every method</h3>
  <ul>
    <li><b>Tune up to the note.</b> If a string is sharp, go below the note and come back up. The string then holds its pitch better.</li>
    <li><b>Turn while the string rings.</b> Small turns. You hear the change happen.</li>
    <li><b>Hum or sing the note.</b> If you can sing the reference and then sing the string, your ear is doing the work.</li>
    <li><b>Finish with a chord.</b> Every method ends at your ear: strum something and adjust any string that sounds sour.</li>
    <li>New strings stretch and go flat for a day or two. Tune, play, tune again.</li>
  </ul>
  <p>Why there are several methods, and what each gets wrong: <a href="/lessons/guitar-tuning-ear.html">Tuning 1: your ear and beats</a>,
  <a href="/lessons/guitar-tuning-methods.html">Tuning 2: fifth-fret, harmonics, octaves</a>,
  <a href="/lessons/guitar-tuning-tuners.html">Tuning 3: tuners and their limits</a>. Something always out however you tune?
  The <a href="/tools/guitar-setup-check.html">Setup Check</a> finds out whether the guitar needs an adjustment.</p>
</div>
